albums.note: Lyrics written from the Nervos Network RFCs, linked on each track. Vocals and music generated with the YuE2 song model; cover art with FLUX 3 Klein. Free to listen to and share for non-commercial use (YuE2 weights are CC BY-NC 4.0).

tracks.title: Scale It Up (2.1)
tracks.lyrics:
[Intro]
Yeah, section two point one
How do you scale it up and let it run

[Verse]
Bitcoin came first, peer-to-peer cash
Ethereum followed with a general purpose stack
Both put a ceiling on what they can pack
Block size, gas limit, keep the nodes intact
You could pump the blocks up, let the fees stay low
Twenty-six gig blocks every ten minutes though
Petabyte a year, only data centres cope
Full nodes drop off, and there goes your hope
Rewards run dry when the last coin's mined
No fees, no miners, security declined
Can't verify yourself, gotta trust some firm
That ain't peer-to-peer, that's the lesson we learn

[Chorus]
Scale it up, don't sell it out
Keep the base layer strong, no doubt
Settle on the chain, move the rest off
Layer one holds it down, layer two takes off
Scale it up, don't sell it out
One global state, that's what it's about

[Verse]
Split it into shards, many chains in a row
Local consensus fast, beacon chain says go
Polkadot's parachains, relay in the middle
But a cross-shard call turns a deal to a riddle
Book a train and a hotel, both gotta go through
Two shards out of sync, now what you gonna do
Yank the contract over, leave a hole behind
DeFi building blocks get hard to combine
One plus N, the meta-chain's got a cap
Composability is where the value's at
Shards work fine when the apps stand alone
But the state worth most wants a single home

[Chorus]
Scale it up, don't sell it out
Keep the base layer strong, no doubt
Settle on the chain, move the rest off
Layer one holds it down, layer two takes off
Scale it up, don't sell it out
One global state, that's what it's about

[Verse]
Layer two, the base chain settles the score
Proofs fly off-chain, instant, cost no more
Alice gets a coffee every morning on the block
Opens up a channel, puts a deposit in stock
Signs a little slip every time she takes a cup
Either side can close it and collect what's up
State channels carry any state you choose
Side-chains run fast but there's trust to lose
Plasma roots its trust in the main chain's floor
Operator goes rogue, you walk out the door
Only the disputes and the settlements land
Decentralised, secure, and it scales as planned

[Chorus]
Scale it up, don't sell it out
Keep the base layer strong, no doubt
Settle on the chain, move the rest off
Layer one holds it down, layer two takes off
Scale it up, don't sell it out
One global state, that's what it's about

[Outro]
Section two point one, that's the plan
Keep it on the base, scale it where you can

tracks.title: Who Pays the Guards
tracks.lyrics:
[Intro]
Positioning paper, two point two point three
Who pays the guards when the rewards run free

[Verse]
Block size capped and the block time's fixed
So space gets scarce and the bidding begins
No loops in the script, so the length tells the cost
More inputs, more outputs, more fees get tossed
The value in the coin is a shared belief
A store of value, that's the whole motif
But the miners get paid in the coin they guard
So the faith has to hold or the fall comes hard
Make a U T X O, pay the fee one time
Then it sits in the state till the end of the line
Pay once, stay forever, that's a sweet little deal
While the miners keep spending just to keep it real

[Chorus]
Who pays the guards when the rewards run dry
City gets rich, gotta fortify
Security budget gotta rise with the prize
Or the walls come down right before your eyes

[Verse]
Hard cap on the supply, the reward goes to zero
Then the fees alone gotta play the hero
Price goes double with rewards in the mix
Hash rate doubles, that's a natural fix
But fees don't care what the coin is worth
They follow block demand, for better or worse
You'd need full blocks every day of the year
And a fee that scales with the price, that's clear
Those are strong assumptions, put it on the list
And there's one more problem that you can't dismiss
Empty mempool and a block full of fees
A miner wants to fork it and take what he sees
Fee sniping, yeah, and it's still not solved
Not without the hard cap getting dissolved

[Chorus]
Who pays the guards when the rewards run dry
City gets rich, gotta fortify
Security budget gotta rise with the prize
Or the walls come down right before your eyes

[Outro]
Good for payments, but for holding it's thin
That's the puzzle that the paper steps in

tracks.title: Propose, Then Commit
tracks.lyrics:
[Intro]
Four point two, consensus on the floor
Nakamoto's good but we're asking for more

[Verse]
Nakamoto consensus, simple and lean
Low overhead, it's a beautiful machine
Two drawbacks though that you can't ignore
Throughput's slow and there's a selfish mining door
So we watch the orphan rate across the net
How well it's connected is the reading we get
Orphans stay low, let the difficulty drop
Blocks come faster and the bandwidth pops
Orphans climb high, pull the pace back down
Every bit of bandwidth gets used in this town

[Chorus]
Propose, then commit, two steps on the beat
Propose, then commit, no bottleneck heat
Count every uncle when you tune the grind
Selfish mining gets left behind

[Verse]
The bottleneck's the block as it moves on the wire
So we split confirmation and the latency's retired
First you propose in the proposal zone
Then you commit in a window that's known
By the time that the block comes knocking at the gate
Every node's seen the transactions, no wait
Now the selfish miner orphans blocks for a gain
Because difficulty never counted that pain
Put the uncles in the difficulty sum
Any mix of strategies, the profit is none
Short attack window from the two-step flow
De facto selfish mining got nowhere to go

[Chorus]
Propose, then commit, two steps on the beat
Propose, then commit, no bottleneck heat
Count every uncle when you tune the grind
Selfish mining gets left behind

[Outro]
Short block interval, security intact
Throughput up, and that's a matter of fact

tracks.title: Do the Work
tracks.source: RFC 1 §4.2.4 Proof of Work vs Proof of Stake
tracks.lyrics:
[Intro]
Four point two point four
Work versus stake, settle the score

[Verse]
Both of them bend to concentrated power
But look how they live in the day to day hour
Proof of work burns real world expense
Slip on your costs and you're over the fence
Gotta innovate, gotta build, gotta spend
Hardware, pools, cheap power to the end
Three things to corner, and they all keep moving
Hard to hold a monopoly when tech keeps improving
Proof of stake pays by the size of the pile
Low cost to run it, just sit there and smile
First mover edge only grows with the scale
A few big stakers and the balance goes pale

[Chorus]
Open door, no permission to ask
Layer one's got one main task
Decentralised, secure, and neutral ground
Do the work, that's how the chain stays sound

[Verse]
Validators hold one power that's unique
They decide who joins, and they don't have to speak
Censor a transaction, shuffle the line
Hard to detect and it's hard to fine
Proof of work's open, come as you are
Early birds get no head start in this bar
They say staking pulls demand for the coin
True at the start while the stakers all join
Then the rate goes flat, in and out the same
Staking by itself is no long term game
Long term holders got three ways to roll
Run a node, or delegate and give up control
Or sit there diluted while the new coins drop
None of that's sweet for the store of value shop

[Chorus]
Open door, no permission to ask
Layer one's got one main task
Decentralised, secure, and neutral ground
Do the work, that's how the chain stays sound

[Outro]
Stake's got a role in the economy, sure
But the base of it all needs an open door

tracks.title: Eaglesong
tracks.lyrics:
[Intro]
Hey, party people, gather round
Let me tell you 'bout a brand new hashing sound
Eaglesong, y'all, Eaglesong

[Verse]
Any node can propose, here's the deal
The block's gotta be valid and the puzzle's gotta be real
The puzzle's tied to the block you bring
So the answer names the block, that's a one of one thing
Bitcoin hashes with a double S H A
Good for them back in the day
But the world built machines for it stack on stack
And a whole lot of them just sit out back
New coin, same hash, and those boxes wake
Rent the hash power, that's a risk to take
Can't predict who's mining, it could swing on a dime
So you want a function that is new this time

[Chorus]
Novel, simple, and secure
Three design goals, that's for sure
Eaglesong, sing it loud
A brand new hash for a brand new crowd

[Verse]
New means nobody tuned it before
No head start waiting at the hardware store
Simple so the chips come easy to build
In the long run, dedicated hardware's a shield
Security's third, and you need a strong case
A hidden weak spot gives one miner the race
So here's how it's made, now follow along
Sponge construction, like Keccak's song
With a permutation out of A R X
Addition, rotation, and xor is next
Wide trail strategy backs the proof
Same one holding up the A E S roof

[Chorus]
Novel, simple, and secure
Three design goals, that's for sure
Eaglesong, sing it loud
A brand new hash for a brand new crowd

[Outro]
First of its kind with all three in one
Eaglesong, y'all, and the party's begun

tracks.title: Land and Houses
tracks.lyrics:
[Intro]
Four point five, the economy
C K Bytes, come and ride with me

[Verse]
One C K Byte is a byte of the state
Hold a thousand, get a thousand, that's the going rate
Make one cell or split it into more
Capacity's the space that you're paying for
Store your data and the bytes get tied
Can't put them in the Dao while they're occupied
That's the cost that you carry, and it's priced by the street
So you free up the state when the price gets steep
Let it go and the bytes come back
Same size as the data that you had in the stack

[Chorus]
Land and houses, land and houses
Bytes are the land, your assets are houses
State rent ticking while you occupy
Lock it in the Dao and the rent slides by

[Verse]
Genesis block, thirty-three point six bill
Eight point four burned and it's burning still
Base issuance halves every four years
All to the miners till the reward disappears
Secondary issuance, steady every year
One point three four four billion, clear
Nervos Dao is the shelter from the rain
Deposit and the dilution's just a name
Hold it like a hard cap, that's the long term play
But the bytes in a cell are the ones that pay
Proportional to space and proportional to time
Not pay once and sit there till the end of the line
Miners get the base and a slice of the second
Sized by the state that's in use, as reckoned
When the base runs out there's still rent to earn
Tied to adoption, not the fee market's turn

[Chorus]
Land and houses, land and houses
Bytes are the land, your assets are houses
State rent ticking while you occupy
Lock it in the Dao and the rent slides by

[Outro]
Demand for many assets into one flows through
And it pays for the guards, that's the point of view

tracks.title: Generate Here, Verify There
tracks.lyrics:
[Intro]
R F C two, four point one
Generate here, verify there, and done

[Verse]
Split the work in two, that's the first design
Generate the state off-chain, verify on the line
Same algorithm, two places to run
Client side builds it, the C K B V M checks it's done
Old state plus input makes a new state fresh
Pack it in a transaction, send it to the mesh
Nodes run it back with the same two things
If the output matches, then the new state sings

[Chorus]
Generate off-chain, verify on
You know the result before the transaction's gone
It passes or it fails, no in between
Certain every time, that's the whole machine

[Verse]
Deterministic, you can see what you made
Before you broadcast, no surprise gets played
Inputs and outputs, written in plain
So nodes see what depends on what in the chain
That means parallel, side by side they go
Workload gets spread and the system don't slow
Pick any language on the client that you please
Fast to develop and it runs with ease
Sometimes the checking is the cheaper deal
Quicksort's N log N to build for real
But checking that it's sorted is a single pass
Binary search, log N, verify in a flash
The more complex the rules, the wider the gap
And that asymmetry is throughput on tap
Zero knowledge proofs fit right in the frame
Generators off-chain is what we call that game

[Chorus]
Generate off-chain, verify on
You know the result before the transaction's gone
It passes or it fails, no in between
Certain every time, that's the whole machine

[Outro]
Details stay with you, privacy's a gain
Only the proof goes down on the chain

tracks.title: Four Fields in a Cell
tracks.lyrics:
[Intro]
Yes yes y'all, and you don't stop
Four fields in a cell, now watch it drop

[Verse]
Capacity, that's the size limit, friend
Everything inside has to fit in the end
Data is the state that you put in the cell
Could be empty, but it's under the limit as well
Type is the script that checks the state
Lock is the script that guards the gate
Lock says who owns it, who can pass it along
Type says the rules so the data ain't wrong

[Chorus]
Capacity, data, type, and lock
Four fields in a cell, now rock
Live cells now, dead cells then
Use it one time and you make it again

[Verse]
A cell can't change, it's set like stone
Used one time, and one time alone
Want an update, here's what you do
Old one's history, you make a new
Same capacity, and it swaps in one go
Old state out, new state in the flow
All the live cells are the knowledge today
All the dead cells are the history, okay
Got ten bytes, you can split it in two
Five and five, now there's more for you
Type runs when the cell is made
Lock runs when it's spent or it's traded
Bring your proof, and if the lock says true
Then the type script rules what you get to do

[Chorus]
Capacity, data, type, and lock
Four fields in a cell, now rock
Live cells now, dead cells then
Use it one time and you make it again

[Verse]
No hard coded crypto in the V M
Bring your own signature, any kind of them
Multisig, M of N, easy to write
Lend out a cell and keep ownership tight
U T X O's clear but the scripts are thin
Account model's easy but the parallel's grim
Cell takes the best of both, you see
A generic state model for you and me

[Chorus]
Capacity, data, type, and lock
Four fields in a cell, now rock
Live cells now, dead cells then
Use it one time and you make it again

tracks.title: Space and Time
tracks.lyrics:
[Intro]
Section five, where the state gets priced
Space and time, yeah, think about it twice

[Verse]
Making new state means the nodes gotta check
Storing that state means disk on their neck
Other chains charge you one time at the door
Then you sit on every node forevermore
Here the cell is the unit, and it's one at a time
Use the space yourself and the interest ain't mine
Could've lent it out, could've earned on the side
That's the cost that you carry for the space you occupied
Bigger and longer means the more you pay
Implicit, no bill coming day by day
No upfront rent that runs out on the clock
No state recycled and a contract in shock

[Chorus]
Space and time, space and time
You pay for the state in space and time
Not computation, it's the state that counts
Capacity holds it in the right amounts

[Verse]
Capacity, type, and lock are state as well
Metadata costs you in every cell
So you make fewer cells and you keep it tight
Capacity efficient, yeah, that's right
Change the data or move who owns
That's a fee, and the miners set the tones
Cycles used and the state you changed
Market finds the price in a healthy range
Cell owners cover fees for the folks they serve
New users walk in with no learning curve
Pay with capacity, that's the native one
Or a user-defined asset if the miner says done
No hard coded payment in the transaction, see
Because the model is the state, not the fee
Forcing native coin is a wall at the gate
Take it down and adoption don't wait

[Chorus]
Space and time, space and time
You pay for the state in space and time
Not computation, it's the state that counts
Capacity holds it in the right amounts

[Outro]
Secure common knowledge, hold it long
That's the main job, and the fee's just a song

tracks.title: Risk Five
tracks.lyrics:
[Intro]
R F C three, the virtual machine
Risk five underneath, keep it clean

[Verse]
The V M's job is to validate
Inputs and outputs, is the transaction straight
Built on risk five, sixty-four bit core
Multiply and divide, then a little bit more
Compressed instructions keep the contract small
No floating point in the set at all
Need a float, pack a soft float in
Deterministic is the way we win
The contract format is a Linux elf
Every tool you know, right there on the shelf

[Chorus]
Main returns zero, that's a pass
Sixty-four bit risk five, built to last
Four megs of memory, single thread
Count every cycle, like the paper said

[Verse]
Four megabytes is the runtime space
Code pages, stack, and the heap in place
Plus the mapped pages from another cell
Runs like a program on a single core shell
Starts at main with arg c and arg v
Return a zero and success is the decree
Might just hand you metadata there
Then syscalls load the rest with care
Single threaded, strict, no atomics required
Bring your own coroutines if that's desired
Any language with a risk five back end
C or Rust, compile it and send
Compile a whole V M, load it as a cell
Run JavaScript or Ruby as well
Cost is the cycles, instruction by instruction
Plus the cells that you read in the function

[Chorus]
Main returns zero, that's a pass
Sixty-four bit risk five, built to last
Four megs of memory, single thread
Count every cycle, like the paper said

[Outro]
Low level machine and it don't pretend
Real hardware rules from beginning to end

tracks.title: Write or Execute
tracks.lyrics:
[Intro]
Write or execute, pick a side
One or the other, nowhere to hide

[Verse]
No M M U in the C K B V M
Like the early C P Us, way back when
Whole block of memory, read, write, and run
Nothing stops a script changing code for fun
Jump to the stack and pretend it's code
That's a wide open door on a dangerous road
Buffer overflow goes writing on the text
Now the script's behaviour is whatever comes next
And the V M itself gets harder to make
Trace cache needs guarding on every write you take
Error prone and it's slow to boot
So here comes a rule to cut it at the root

[Chorus]
Write or execute, never both
Every page takes a single oath
Break the rule and you catch a fault
Write or execute, that's the vault

[Verse]
Four K pages, aligned on the line
Zero, then four K, eight K, every time
Each page carries a flag for the two
Writable or executable, one will do
Before an instruction, check the page can run
Before a write, check the page allows one
Break either rule and a page fault lands
That's the law, and that's how it stands
On boot every page starts writable, then
The load sections marked to execute, amen
An elf with a section that's both gets denied
Returns with an error, no free ride
Code not aligned, stretch it to the edge
Round to the page, that's the pledge
Return oriented tricks could still get through
But the easy mistakes get stopped for you

[Chorus]
Write or execute, never both
Every page takes a single oath
Break the rule and you catch a fault
Write or execute, that's the vault

[Outro]
Simpler machine and a safer script
And the just in time compiler's better equipped

tracks.title: Headers First
tracks.lyrics:
[Intro]
R F C four, how the blocks come in
Headers first, let the sync begin

[Verse]
Three stages, and they go in a row
Cheapest check first, that's the way to go
Connect the header, check the format and the work
Five percent effort for a ninety-five perk
Then download the block and check it's whole
Then accept it in the chain, that's the final goal
A block starts unknown before the header's read
Fail any step and it's invalid instead
Connected, downloaded, accepted at last
Never ahead of the parent in the past
If the parent goes bad then the children go too
So you don't waste work on a branch that's through

[Chorus]
Connect the header, download the block
Accept it in the chain, tick tock
Headers first, least cost on top
Most work wins, and the sync don't stop

[Verse]
Alice meets Bob and she samples her chain
Latest ten blocks, then she steps back again
Two, four, eight, with the gaps getting wide
That's the locator, sends it to his side
Bob finds the block that they both agree
Sends the headers from there to his tip, you see
Same genesis, so there's always one
Now the downloading stage can run
Sliding window, split it into stripes
Scheduled over peers with the right block types
Merkle root wrong, don't call the block bad
Blacklist the sender, that's the peer you had
Or a liar could poison your status tree
Then accept with the context, the heavy degree
Roll back the tip and verify the line
If it fails, restore the best chain, fine

[Chorus]
Connect the header, download the block
Accept it in the chain, tick tock
Headers first, least cost on top
Most work wins, and the sync don't stop

[Outro]
Tip moves on, so announce it to the crew
Compact block if there's one, headers if a few

tracks.title: Machine Mode
tracks.lyrics:
[Intro]
R F C five, the privileged mode
Opt in only, it's off in the code

[Verse]
One contract at a time, so you don't need rings
But a privileged model brings a few good things
An M M U for the contracts that grow
Dynamic memory, and the bad access? No
Beginners trade cycles for a safer run
Pros who want it lean can leave it undone
Closed by default, it's your call to make
Ignore it completely for the cycles' sake

[Chorus]
Machine mode, user mode
Two levels in the privileged code
M ret, and you step on down
Sixty-four entries when the fault comes round

[Verse]
C S R instructions, straight from the spec
Read and write registers, keep it correct
Not every register, just the ones for the trap
S T vec holds the handler on the map
Touch the others, illegal instruction's the call
Handle it how you like, that's all
Starts in machine mode, free to roam
User mode's limited, a smaller home
No C S R, no machine mode page
No executing where the flag's not engaged
Set your metadata up, then drop with M ret
Now the trap function's what catches the threat

[Verse]
T L B, sixty-four entries deep
Each one a page, four K to keep
One way associative, here's the trick
Same last six bits and one gets kicked
Switch your privilege level, the whole thing's flushed
Built on the first page fault, never rushed
Stay in machine mode, you may never meet
Once it's up, it stays on the beat

[Chorus]
Machine mode, user mode
Two levels in the privileged code
M ret, and you step on down
Sixty-four entries when the fault comes round

[Outro]
Opt in, opt out, it's yours to decide
The V M's got it waiting on the side

albums.note: Lyrics written from the Nervos Network RFCs, linked on each track. Vocals and music generated with the YuE2 song model; cover art with FLUX 3 Klein. Free to listen to and share for non-commercial use (YuE2 weights are CC BY-NC 4.0).

tracks.title: Complete Binary Tree
tracks.lyrics:
[Intro]
Hey y'all, we got a tree to build
Complete and binary, every level filled

[Verse]
Got a static list, need a single root
C B M T is the way we compute
Every level's full, 'cept maybe the last
And the nodes sit left, yeah, packed in fast
It's a full tree too, so here's the news
Every node that ain't a leaf has two
Fewer hashes than the other trees around
That's the reason that we lay it on down

[Chorus]
Top to the bottom, left to the right
Count from zero and you count it right
Complete binary, keep it tight
One little array and the tree's in sight

[Verse]
Number every node as you go on through
Root comes first, and the rest ensue
With N items, here's the size that's done
The array's two N, then you minus one
Item number I, where's it gonna be
At I plus N minus one, you see
Parent of a node, take one away
Then you half it down, that's the play
Sibling? Add one, x-or one, minus one
Children at two I plus one, plus two, and done
No items at all? Then the tree is bare
Root's all zeros, nothing there

[Chorus]
Top to the bottom, left to the right
Count from zero and you count it right
Complete binary, keep it tight
One little array and the tree's in sight

[Outro]
Transactions root, that's the job it's got
One flat array, and it saves a lot

tracks.title: Prove It
tracks.lyrics:
[Intro]
You say it's in there? Prove it
You say it's in there? Prove it

[Verse]
Got a root on the chain and a claim in your hand
One item or more, now here's the plan
Walk from the leaf on up to the top
Grab every sibling at every stop
Leave out the nodes that are already in the path
You can work those out, that's simple math
Just the siblings needed, nothing more
The nodes you can't work out, that's the core

[Chorus]
Prove it, prove it, walk it to the root
Siblings on the path, that's all you compute
Prove it, prove it, highest index first
Hash it up together till the root is rehearsed

[Verse]
Now the order matters when you pack the proof
Descending order, that's the truth
Makes the building and the checking plain
A simple little loop, again and again
And the index of the item's gotta come along
'Cause the hash don't know where it belongs
Two parts in the proof when you send it through
The indexes and the nodes come too

[Verse]
To check it, take your leaves and the nodes you got
Put 'em in a queue, largest index on top
Pop a node, find its sibling in the line
If it's next in the queue, then that works fine
If it ain't, take a node from the proof's stack
Hash the pair to the parent, push it back
When the parent is the root, then the walk is done
If it matches the root, then the proof has won

[Chorus]
Prove it, prove it, walk it to the root
Siblings on the path, that's all you compute
Prove it, prove it, highest index first
Hash it up together till the root is rehearsed

tracks.title: Eclipse
tracks.lyrics:
[Intro]
Lights out, lights out
Somebody's blocking out the sun

[Verse]
Open network, anybody joins
No permission, no tickets, no coins
That's the beauty, but it cuts two ways
Bad nodes walk in too these days
Here's the trick that they call eclipse
Fill every slot till the true view slips
All your peer connections in the attacker's hands
Now you only see what the attacker plans

[Chorus]
Eclipse, eclipse, don't let 'em block the sun
Keep the good peers close and the bad ones on the run
Store 'em, score 'em, show the low ones out
That's what the peer to peer is all about

[Verse]
Cheap to pull and the damage runs deep
Take a node down while the network sleeps
Steer its mining power where they like
Or set it up for a double spend strike
Bitcoin saw it, Ethereum too
There's a paper on it, tells you what to do
Some of those defences are already live
So we bring 'em on over, help the network thrive

[Verse]
Three little rules and you write 'em down
Number one, store every peer in town
Much as you can, keep the info deep
Number two, keep score, don't sleep
Good behaviour, bad behaviour, all the time
Number three, keep the high scores on the line
And the low scores, well, they gotta go
Evict 'em out and on with the show

[Chorus]
Eclipse, eclipse, don't let 'em block the sun
Keep the good peers close and the bad ones on the run
Store 'em, score 'em, show the low ones out
That's what the peer to peer is all about

tracks.title: Keep Score
tracks.lyrics:
[Intro]
Ladies and gentlemen, on the scoreboard tonight
Every peer gets a number, alright

[Verse]
Every peer starts out at the initial score
Then we watch what they do, and we watch some more
A set of behaviours, each one's got a price
The scoring schema, cut and sliced
Connected? That's a plus ten for you
Timeout? Minus ten, that's due
Sync and relay tell the network layer
What they saw from every player

[Chorus]
Keep score, keep score, everybody's on the board
Do it right for a long time, get your reward
Keep score, keep score, drop below the line
Under ban score, baby, you're out of time

[Verse]
Three kinds of moves that a peer can make
First is correct, give a little, not a cake
'Cause a bad one's nice till the day it strikes
So the credit's slow, earn it over nights
Second is the kind that the network might cause
A drop, a timeout, a ping that's lost
Can't tell if they meant it, so we stay polite
A little minus, keep it light

[Verse]
Third is the kind that breaks the rules
Bad encoding, an invalid block, those fools
An invalid transaction on the wire
That's a big minus, now the heat gets higher
Peer one keeps asking for the same old block
Duplicated request, minus fifty on the clock
Falls below the ban score, disconnect and ban
None of this is consensus, so tune it where you can

[Chorus]
Keep score, keep score, everybody's on the board
Do it right for a long time, get your reward
Keep score, keep score, drop below the line
Under ban score, baby, you're out of time

tracks.title: Anchor Peers
tracks.lyrics:
[Intro]
Drop the anchor, drop the anchor
Before you sail, drop the anchor

[Verse]
Here's how they got you on the restart, friend
Stuff your address book end to end
Bad addresses, then they wait a while
You reboot, and they start to smile
You pick from the book and you dial 'em in
If all your outbound's theirs, they win
So when we start up, here's the fix
A little bit of old and a random mix

[Chorus]
Anchor first, then random from the store
Different network group than the ones before
Score above the try score, that's the door
And the boot nodes waiting if there ain't no more

[Verse]
Step one, count your outbound friends
Under the anchor number? That's where it begins
Look at who you talked to recently
Take the highest score, that's your anchor, see
Got your anchors, or the recent list is bare
Pick at random from the peer store there
But it's gotta beat the try score clean
And a different network group from the ones on screen

[Verse]
Nothing fits? Then the boot nodes play
Keep on going till you're full all day
Now the sync goes quiet, nothing coming through
Flip the switch, try a new peer or two
Extra outbound till the messages flow
Then evict the useless, let the extras go
Attacker needs the anchors, highest score in the book
And every random pick, that's a long, long look

[Chorus]
Anchor first, then random from the store
Different network group than the ones before
Score above the try score, that's the door
And the boot nodes waiting if there ain't no more

tracks.title: Who Gets In
tracks.source: RFC 7 Inbound peers, feelers and the peer store
tracks.lyrics:
[Intro]
The club is full, the line is long
Who gets in? Sing along

[Verse]
Inbound slots are all filled tight
New peer knocking in the middle of the night
Don't just slam it, don't just let 'em through
Run the eviction test, here's what you do
Everybody inside is a candidate now
Then we start protecting, here's how
Take out the ones with the highest score
Then the lowest ping, walk 'em from the floor

[Chorus]
Who gets in, who gets out
Protect the good ones, that's what it's about
Biggest group, lowest score
That's the one we show the door

[Verse]
Then the ones who talked to us most recently
Then half of what's left by seniority
Longest connected, they can stay
Things an attacker can't fake any day
Now group what's left by the network group
Find the biggest crowd in the loop
Lowest score in that group gets tossed
If the group is empty, the new peer's lost

[Verse]
When the outbound's full, every few minutes more
Send a feeler out to a peer in the store
One we never called, just to see
Connect, shake hands, disconnect, we're free
And the peer store's got a limit too
When it's full and there's somebody new
Biggest group, not seen in a while
Lowest score there, check the file
If the new one's better, then they trade
If it ain't, the new one's not getting saved

[Chorus]
Who gets in, who gets out
Protect the good ones, that's what it's about
Biggest group, lowest score
That's the one we show the door

tracks.title: Molecule
tracks.lyrics:
[Intro]
Byte by byte, y'all
Byte by byte

[Verse]
Two formats on the C K B
Molecule and J S O N, you see
J S O N is for the R P C
Molecule's the one for you and me
Canonical, one way to write
Zero copy, read it in flight
Every type's either fixed or it's dynamic size
Header numbers little-endian, no surprise

[Chorus]
Byte, array, and struct
Fixed size, nothing gets tucked
No overhead, side by side
Molecule, enjoy the ride

[Verse]
Start with a byte, and a byte is a byte
Zero zero, that's alright
Array's got an inner type and a length that's set
Size is the two multiplied, you bet
Three bytes: one, two, three
Zero one, zero two, zero three, easy
A thirty-two bit number, little end in front
Oh one oh two oh three oh four, here's the stunt
It goes four, three, two, one in the line
Low byte first, every time

[Verse]
Struct is a bunch of fixed fields in a row
In the order you declared, that's how they go
Size is the sum, there's nothing in between
No padding, no gaps, keep it clean
A byte then a number, A B, then the four
One two three in the little-endian store
A B, oh three, oh two, oh one, zero zero
Five bytes flat, and the struct's the hero

[Chorus]
Byte, array, and struct
Fixed size, nothing gets tucked
No overhead, side by side
Molecule, enjoy the ride

tracks.title: Fix-Vec, Dyn-Vec
tracks.lyrics:
[Intro]
Fix-vec, dyn-vec, what's the deal
Look inside and the type's revealed

[Verse]
Two kinds of vectors in the molecule game
Fixed and dynamic, and here's how they're named
Look at the item sitting inside
Fixed-size item? Fix-vec's the ride
Anything else and it's dyn-vec time
Both are dynamic size, keep that in mind
Fix-vec takes two steps, that's all
Write the count of items, then the items fall

[Chorus]
Fix-vec, count then the items in a row
Dyn-vec, size, then the offsets, then they go
Table's a dyn-vec with a fixed length, so
Size, offsets, fields, now you know

[Verse]
Count's a thirty-two bit little-endian number
Empty fix-vec, four zero bytes, no wonder
One byte, one two, here's what you see
Oh one and three zeros, then the one two, easy
Eight bytes in, then it's oh eight up top
Three zeros, then the eight bytes drop

[Verse]
Dyn-vec's three steps, listen up
Full size in bytes, that's the first in the cup
Then an offset for every item you hold
Then the items themselves, all told
Empty dyn-vec, the size is four
Just the header and nothing more
Table's the same, but the field count's set
Size, then offsets, then the fields, you bet
In the order declared, every field gets a spot
Even the fixed ones, like it or not

[Chorus]
Fix-vec, count then the items in a row
Dyn-vec, size, then the offsets, then they go
Table's a dyn-vec with a fixed length, so
Size, offsets, fields, now you know

tracks.title: Option, Union
tracks.lyrics:
[Intro]
Maybe something, maybe not
One of many, that's the plot

[Verse]
Option's dynamic, here's the game
Empty or full, it ain't the same
If it's empty, there's nothing there
Zero bytes, the cupboard's bare
If it's got something, just write the thing
Same size as the item that you bring
No extra tag, no flag to see
The length alone tells you what it'll be

[Chorus]
Option, nothing or the item straight
Union, type id, then the freight
Maybe something, one of some
Molecule, and the bytes go drum

[Verse]
None is empty, not a byte
Some with an empty vector, that's four, alright
Oh four, zero, zero, zero on the line
The empty dyn-vec header, fine

[Verse]
Union's dynamic, two steps through
First the item type id, that's the clue
Thirty-two bits, little-endian, friend
It's the index of the item, zero on the front end
Then you serialize what's inside
Whatever type the id implied
First type in the list is the Byte Three
Four zero bytes, then one two, three four, five six, see
Second in the list, then it's oh one first
Then the item follows, unrehearsed
Third in the list starts oh two, then
The vector that's inside, and count again

[Chorus]
Option, nothing or the item straight
Union, type id, then the freight
Maybe something, one of some
Molecule, and the bytes go drum

[Outro]
Fixed or dynamic, now you know the set
Byte by byte, no sweat

tracks.title: Partial Loading
tracks.lyrics:
[Intro]
Can't take it all? Take a piece
Partial loading, if you please

[Verse]
Script's in the V M, world's outside
Needs a way to reach and a way to ride
Syscalls, that's the telephone line
To the transaction, the chain, the header, fine
No custom instructions, standard risk five
Keeps the tools all working, keeps the thing alive
And every call but exit plays the same game
Three arguments with the same three names

[Chorus]
Address, length, and offset
Take what fits, and the rest ain't lost yet
Full size comes back in the length you set
Partial loading, no regret

[Verse]
Address is the buffer where the data lands
Length is a pointer, sixty-four bit in your hands
Going in, it's how big your buffer's got
Coming out, it's the size of the whole lot
Offset's where you wanna start the read
Now here's the steps, and here's the speed
Read the size that the length points to
Full size is the data minus offset, true

[Verse]
Real size is the smaller of the two
Write that much to the address for you
Then full size goes back in the length
Return a zero, that's success, that's strength
Memory's tight? Then read it in bites
Chunk by chunk through the days and nights
And here's a trick, give a null for the address
And a zero length, and you get the size, no less
Not a byte gets copied, just the count
Now you know the full amount

[Chorus]
Address, length, and offset
Take what fits, and the rest ain't lost yet
Full size comes back in the length you set
Partial loading, no regret

tracks.title: E-Call
tracks.lyrics:
[Intro]
Operator, operator
Get me the chain on the line

[Verse]
Six arguments, here's where they go
Registers A zero through A five, you know
Each one's a word, so it holds a number
Or it holds a pointer, there's no blunder
Syscall number goes in A seven
Then you fire the e-call, straight to heaven
Don't need all six? Then fill what you need
The rest stay zero, guaranteed

[Chorus]
Put it in A seven, make the e-call
Answer comes back in A zero, y'all
Or it's written in the memory where you point
Syscall party, rock the joint

[Verse]
Two ways back when the call is through
A return value in A zero for you
Or the data's written where your pointer said
And your normal instructions read it instead
Wrap it in a C function, make it neat
Six arguments every time, on the beat
Exit only needs the one, that's fine
Zero out the others, hold the line

[Verse]
Exit's the only way out the door
Give it a code, and there ain't no more
The V M stops right there with that return
It don't come back, that's the thing to learn
Load transaction hash, load the whole transaction
Molecule encoded, that's the action
Load script hash, load the script that's run
Partial loading works for every one

[Chorus]
Put it in A seven, make the e-call
Answer comes back in A zero, y'all
Or it's written in the memory where you point
Syscall party, rock the joint

tracks.title: Load Cell
tracks.source: RFC 9 Loading cells, headers and witnesses
tracks.lyrics:
[Intro]
Load it up, load it up
Index and source, load it up

[Verse]
Load cell takes an index and a source
Plus address, length, and offset, of course
Source one is the inputs, two is the outs
Three is the dep cells, no doubts
There's a special flag for the group you're in
Just the cells with the script you're running
Whole cell comes back in molecule, friend
Index out of bounds? That's a one in the end

[Chorus]
Load cell, load cell, tell me what you see
By field, by data, bring it back to me
Wrong source, the V M halts, that's the key
Out of bounds is a one, missing is a two, agree

[Verse]
Load cell by field when you don't need it all
Zero is capacity, that's the call
One is the data hash, two is the lock
Three is the lock hash, tick tock
Four is the type and five is its hash
Six is occupied capacity, in a flash
Ask for a type that the cell ain't got
Get a two back, that's the spot

[Verse]
Load cell data gives you just the data part
Load as code, now that's a work of art
Maps it in memory and marks it to run
Four K aligned or the V M's done
Load header from an input, a dep, or header deps
Hash in the header deps, mind your steps
Load witness by the index, source is a hint
And debug takes a string and gives the log a print

[Chorus]
Load cell, load cell, tell me what you see
By field, by data, bring it back to me
Wrong source, the V M halts, that's the key
Out of bounds is a one, missing is a two, agree

tracks.title: Forty-Three Rounds
tracks.lyrics:
[Intro]
Forty-three rounds, y'all
Forty-three rounds, count 'em

[Verse]
Eaglesong's a sponge, so here's the thing
A permutation and three numbers that it brings
Rate and capacity, and a delimiter byte
Two five six, two five six, oh six, that's right
Stick the delimiter on the end of what you got
Chop it into chunks of the rate, that's the lot
State starts at zero, five twelve bits wide
Absorb every chunk with an x-or on the top side

[Chorus]
Forty-three rounds, and the eagle sings
Addition, rotation, x-or, three things
Absorb it, then squeeze it, that's the sponge
Two fifty-six bits when the work is done

[Verse]
After every chunk, run the permutation through
Then you squeeze out the output, that's what you do
A R X, and that's all we use
Add, rotate, x-or, nothing to confuse
Thirty-two bit words and there's sixteen in the state
One round function, forty-three times straight
Four little steps in every round
Listen up close and I'll break it down

[Verse]
Step one, the bit matrix, ones and zeros
Tells you which words to x-or, those are the heroes
Step two, circulant, every word in the set
X-or with itself rotated twice, you bet
Step three, inject the constants in
Different every word and every round we spin
Step four, add, rotate, add, in eight little pairs
Right to the left, then they spin eight opposite squares
Then the left to the right, and that's the only place
Where the modular addition shows its face

[Chorus]
Forty-three rounds, and the eagle sings
Addition, rotation, x-or, three things
Absorb it, then squeeze it, that's the sponge
Two fifty-six bits when the work is done

[Outro]
Proof of work on the C K B
Eaglesong, y'all, one two three

albums.note: Lyrics written from the Nervos Network RFCs, linked on each track. Vocals and music generated with the YuE2 song model; cover art with FLUX 3 Klein. Free to listen to and share for non-commercial use (YuE2 weights are CC BY-NC 4.0).

tracks.title: Low Capacity
tracks.lyrics:
[Intro]
Small device, big chain
Only send me what's mine

[Verse]
Smartphone, browser extension in my hand
Embedded device, low capacity, understand
Can't verify the whole chain, that's a fact
Just check that the headers connect, stay intact
Trust the block of the highest difficulty
The transactions inside it are valid to me
Without this I'm downloading every block
Every broadcast transaction, round the clock
Then throwing most of it away
Slow sync, wasted bandwidth, memory to pay

[Chorus]
Set the filter, set the filter
Only what I want comes through
Bloom on the line, peer by peer
Set the filter, cut the queue

[Verse]
Set filter message, three fields in the frame
Filter, num hashes, hash seed, that's the name
Filter's a bit field, byte-aligned in size
Thirty-six thousand bytes is the max, no lies
Num hashes, twenty at the top
Holds ten thousand items before the false ones pop
One in a million, false positive rate
Hash seed's a random offset, set it straight
H one is the low half, H two is the high
Seed plus H one plus N times H two, try
Mod the filter size and you land on a bit
Soon as the peer gets the message, that's it
Restricts what it broadcasts to the ones that match
Every connection, its own filter to attach

[Chorus]
Set the filter, set the filter
Only what I want comes through
Bloom on the line, peer by peer
Set the filter, cut the queue

[Outro]
R F C eleven, marked withdrawn
Small device, big chain, the idea lives on

tracks.title: Match Found
tracks.source: RFC 11 Filter matching, AddFilter, ClearFilter, FilteredBlock
tracks.lyrics:
[Intro]
Test it, test it
Once it hits, we stop

[Verse]
Every broadcast transaction gets a test
Against the filter, here's the order, no rest
First the hash of the transaction itself
Then each cell input, pull it off the shelf
Hash of the previous output, check
Then every cell output, next on deck
Lock hash and type hash of the script
Find one match and the rest gets skipped
Nothing hits? Then there's no match
Algorithm aborts on the very first catch

[Chorus]
Match found, match found
Send it down the line
No match, no sound
That one isn't mine

[Verse]
Add filter when you got more to track
Bitwise OR on the filter, stack on stack
Got to set one first before you add
Can't be bigger than the one you had
Keeps the connection open, saves the pain
Of sending a whole new filter again
Clear filter, no arguments at all
Tells the peer to drop it, end of call
After you set it, there's more they do
Filtered block message coming to you
In place of block and compact block too
Header's standard, same as you knew
Transactions, each with an index tied
And hashes, a Merkle branch on the side

[Chorus]
Match found, match found
Send it down the line
No match, no sound
That one isn't mine

[Outro]
Molecule on the wire, byte by byte
Only what matches comes in tonight

tracks.title: Seed Nodes
tracks.lyrics:
[Intro]
First time up, nobody knows me
Who do I call?

[Verse]
Client starts and the address list is bare
Peer store empty, nobody there
First move, send the D N S requests
Seed hostnames in the client, that's the nest
Learn the addresses of the other peers
That's the bootstrap stage, switch the gears
If the D N S fails, every single try
Fall back on the list that's hard-coded inside
Seed addresses, built right in
Only used when the D N S can't win

[Chorus]
Seed nodes, seed nodes
High uptime, many roads
Get what I need and I let them go
Don't overload the seed nodes

[Verse]
Seed nodes been up for a long, long time
Many connections down many a line
Once I got enough addresses stored
Close those connections, don't hog the board
Modelled on the Satoshi client way
With a few differences, here's what they say
Version number rides in the get nodes call
Nodes message broadcasts the connected, all
Periodically, to everyone you know
Multi-address is the format, though
And it must not have the P two P segment in
That's misbehaviour, low score for the sin

[Chorus]
Seed nodes, seed nodes
High uptime, many roads
Get what I need and I let them go
Don't overload the seed nodes

[Outro]
Empty list to a full address book
D N S first, then the seeds, that's the hook

tracks.title: Announce
tracks.lyrics:
[Intro]
Outbound only
Ask once, hear once

[Verse]
Three conditions before I send get nodes
All got to hold, that's how it goes
One, it's an outbound connection, mine
That's for the fingerprinting, hold the line
Two, their version's bigger than the preset
Three, my stored addresses ain't there yet
Under the threshold, a thousand by default
Version, count, and a listen port, that's all

[Chorus]
Announce true, announce false
One's a reply and one's a pulse
Break the rules and the score gets hit
Announce, announce, that's the bit

[Verse]
You get my get nodes, you send nodes back
First time and inbound, that's the track
Announce set false, because it's a reply
Only one of those per ask, don't try
At regular intervals, here's the other one
Broadcast your connected nodes to everyone
Announce set true, that's the broadcast kind
Receive it and relay the routable ones you find
Only the first broadcast can go past ten
Announce threshold, don't flood it again
Each node in the message, three addresses max
Max node addresses, those are the facts
The announce field tells the two apart
So the punishment rules can be smart

[Chorus]
Announce true, announce false
One's a reply and one's a pulse
Break the rules and the score gets hit
Announce, announce, that's the bit

[Outro]
Discovery message, the payload's a union
Get nodes or nodes, pick one, keep moving

tracks.title: Block Template
tracks.lyrics:
[Intro]
Don't keep me in the dark
Show me the whole block

[Verse]
Old get work just handed out a header
Miner solving blind, nothing better
Kept in the dark, no say in the block
No influence on what's in stock
Get block template flips the script
Whole block structure, fully equipped
Sent to the miner to customise
Assemble it, audit it with your own eyes
Modify it, maybe, before you hash
Decentralised blocks, security that lasts

[Chorus]
Give me the template, I'll build the block
Give me the template, I run the clock
Version, difficulty, number, parent hash
Give me the template, then I send it back

[Verse]
J S O N R P C, three arguments in
Cycles limit, bytes limit, max version
Leave them out, consensus default's the call
Server should respect them, not required at all
So the client checks what the template brings
Back comes an object with a list of things
Version, difficulty in hex, current time
Number of the block and the parent hash line
Cellbase, required, it's always there
Commit transactions with their data laid bare
Hash and data, and maybe cycles too
Required flag true means it's got to go through
Depends tells you which ones come before
Proposal transactions, short I Ds, more
Work I D, if they hand you one
Send it back with the block when you're done

[Chorus]
Give me the template, I'll build the block
Give me the template, I run the clock
Version, difficulty, number, parent hash
Give me the template, then I send it back

[Outro]
Submit block, molecule bytes in hex
Work I D with it, on to the next

tracks.title: Max Block Cycles
tracks.source: RFC 14 Consensus change and loading cycles
tracks.lyrics:
[Intro]
Everything halts
Everything halts, or it errors

[Verse]
The V M's flexible, free to run
Loops and branches, any control flow, done
So we need some rules to keep it clean
Malicious script with an infinite loop, that's mean
Introduce cycles, here's the cost
Every instruction, every syscall, tossed
Onto the meter, each one consumes
Add it all up for the block, no room
Past the limit and the block's rejected
That's how the network stays protected

[Chorus]
Max block cycles, that's the ceiling
Sum of the scripts, no more dealing
Go over and the block gets dropped
Max block cycles, that's where it stops

[Verse]
It's a scalar field in the chain spec now
Consensus rule, hard limit, here's how
Sum of the cycles of all scripts in the block
Can't exceed it, that's the lock
But there's no limit on a single transaction
No cap on one script, free in its action
Long as the whole block stays below
Use what you want, go fast, go slow
Guaranteed that every script will halt
Or end in an error state, by default
Risk five costs come from real hardware
Syscalls from benchmarks, measured with care
Loading the binary, there's a charge on that too
Quarter of a cycle per byte, coming through
Fractions round up, so here's the sum
Thirty and a quarter becomes thirty-one
Ship it small, that's what it's for
Big binary attacks get shown the door

[Chorus]
Max block cycles, that's the ceiling
Sum of the scripts, no more dealing
Go over and the block gets dropped
Max block cycles, that's where it stops

[Outro]
Everything halts
Everything halts, or it errors

tracks.title: One Cycle
tracks.lyrics:
[Intro]
What's it cost? What's it cost?
Read me the price list

[Verse]
Most instructions cost one cycle flat
But some of them don't, so look at that
Jump and branch, that's three a go
Branches cost more than the normal flow
Load a double word, store one, two
Sixty-four bit system, that's the cheap one for you
Load a word, a half, or a byte, that's three
Smaller values cost more, you see
Memory access ain't the normal rate
More than a plain instruction, straight

[Chorus]
One for the normal, three for the branch
Five to multiply, thirty-two to divide
Five hundred for the e-call, that's the fee
Count them cycles, count with me

[Verse]
Multiply's five, all five kinds
Divide's thirty-two, keep that in mind
Remainder too, same thirty-two
Much more expensive, that's the view
E-call, five hundred, e-break the same
Syscall's got two parts in the game
Bookkeeping first, the complex bit
That's the five hundred, pay for it
Then a plain memory copy, cheap to run
Quarter cycle a byte and it's done
Round the fraction up at the end
Just like the loading, same rule, friend
Looks a lot like the numbers you find
In modern computer architecture, same kind

[Chorus]
One for the normal, three for the branch
Five to multiply, thirty-two to divide
Five hundred for the e-call, that's the fee
Count them cycles, count with me

[Outro]
Hard rules now, written in the R F C
Might move into consensus, we'll see

tracks.title: Medium or Store
tracks.source: RFC 15 §2 The crypto-economics design of Bitcoin
tracks.lyrics:
[Intro]
Two kinds of users on the same chain
Which one pays?

[Verse]
Medium of exchange, that's the first kind
Don't hold the coin, just the transfer in mind
Buy it just in time and sell it just the same
Don't care about the price, only the fee in the game
Store of value, that's the other side
Hold it for years, let the fee cost slide
Spread it over time, it's nothing much
Care about security, decentralised and such
If it's easy to attack, the value's gone
If it's centralised, counter-party risk is on

[Chorus]
Medium or store, medium or store
One moves through, one holds for more
Who compensates the miners in the long run?
Medium or store, when the coins are done

[Verse]
Hard cap means when the last coin's mined
Fees alone pay the miners, that's the design
Open question if that can last
Store of value networks don't transact fast
The movers got little exposure to the risk
Won't pay for security, in and out, brisk
The holders are exposed for a long, long while
Willing to pay, but no transactions to file
And the hash power guards more than this block
Every block before it's under that lock
One-time payments for an ongoing guard
Not sustainable, that's the hard part
So inflation fits the store of value way
Indirect payment, the ones who benefit pay
In proportion to the time they stay

[Chorus]
Medium or store, medium or store
One moves through, one holds for more
Who compensates the miners in the long run?
Medium or store, when the coins are done

tracks.title: Store of Assets
tracks.lyrics:
[Intro]
Not just one coin
Many assets, one platform

[Verse]
Smart contract platform issues tokens out
Ownership of assets, that's what they're about
Own communities, own markets too
Value independent of the platform, true
But they lean on the platform all the same
To process transactions and secure the game
Bitcoin's a single asset platform, see
Smart contracts, multi-asset, plenty
Store of value was the Bitcoin phrase
Store of assets is the one we raise

[Chorus]
Store of assets, store of assets
Security's got to grow with what it protects
Or the platform is the ceiling on the value next
Store of assets, store of assets

[Verse]
If the assets grow and the guard stays small
Double spend pays, attack the consensus, all
None of the platforms today built this way
Tokens for transactions, or for stake, they say
Either way the asset value climbs
And the miner's income stays behind
Every platform's an ecosystem inside
Independent projects, side by side
Security is public goods for them all
Needs a clear mechanism, or it'll stall
Capture the success of the whole ecosystem
Turn asset demand into miner revenue, listen
Raise the value of the native token paid
Otherwise there's a ceiling, and the liquidity fades
When transactions can't be protected enough
Demand for the asset dries right up

[Chorus]
Store of assets, store of assets
Security's got to grow with what it protects
Or the platform is the ceiling on the value next
Store of assets, store of assets

[Outro]
Decentralised, multi-asset, smart contract too
Got to be a store of assets to make it through

tracks.title: Pay Once, Occupy Forever
tracks.source: RFC 15 §5 Decentralization and the need for bounded state
tracks.lyrics:
[Intro]
Pay once
Occupy forever? Nah

[Verse]
Gold held value for thousands of years
Neutral, no censor, no confiscation fears
For a chain that means a low barrier in
Run a full node, anybody can spin
Smart contract full node costs more to run
Protect that cost or decentralised is done
Bitcoin throttles bandwidth, Ethereum compute
But the global state keeps growing, that's the dispute
Bitcoin's state is the U T X O set
Once one's made it sits there free, no debt

[Chorus]
Pay once, occupy forever
That's the model that we got to sever
Bound the state and let the market price it
Pay once, occupy forever? Not likely

[Verse]
Ethereum charges fixed gas to store
Refund when you clear it, but there's more
Size ain't bounded, nor the growth rate
No certainty on the full node weight
One-time revenue, but the storage cost
Sits on the miners and the nodes, time lost
Gas was made for pricing computation
Why price storage with it? No explanation
State rent's the leading plan on their side
Pay by the size or the contract hibernates, denied
But a token contract's many users deep
Hard to coordinate who pays the keep
Three goals, then, for the state we hold
Bounded growth, so the cost's controlled
Market sets the price to expand or free
And revenue keeps flowing to the miners, steadily

[Chorus]
Pay once, occupy forever
That's the model that we got to sever
Bound the state and let the market price it
Pay once, occupy forever? Not likely

[Outro]
Bandwidth, computation, now the state
Constrain it and price it, before it's too late

tracks.title: Sixty, Thirty-Five, Five
tracks.source: RFC 15 §6 Native tokens, issuance and the NervosDAO
tracks.lyrics:
[Intro]
Sixty, thirty-five, five
Watch the issuance divide

[Verse]
C K Byte, common knowledge byte
Cell capacity, a piece of the state, right
Alice got a thousand, makes a thousand byte cell
Or a few that add up, just as well
Four bytes for capacity, sixty-four for the lock
One twenty-eight for state on the block
One ninety-six occupied, room to grow
Up to a thousand, now you know
Smallest unit is the C K Shannon
A hundred million to a byte, that's canon

[Chorus]
Sixty to the miners, thirty-five to the Dao
Five gets burned till the community says how
That's the example, that's the split
Follows where the bytes all sit

[Verse]
Two issuances, the base is first
Finite supply, halves about every four years
All of it to miners till it's mined out
Secondary's constant, there's no doubt
Built to collect the state rent due
Targeted inflation, two steps through
Step one, inflation tax on everyone holding
Storing state? That's your rent unfolding
Step two, the ones not storing state
Deposit in the Dao and it compensates
Dao takes a share of the secondary flow
Makes up for the dilution, so
Say sixty percent of the bytes store state
Thirty-five in the Dao, five liquid, wait
Sixty to the miners, thirty-five to the locked
Five for the community, burned till they've talked
Long term holders in the Dao don't feel it
Like a hard cap token, that's how they see it

[Chorus]
Sixty to the miners, thirty-five to the Dao
Five gets burned till the community says how
That's the example, that's the split
Follows where the bytes all sit

tracks.title: Same Side
tracks.source: RFC 15 §7 Aligning interests and first class assets
tracks.lyrics:
[Intro]
Everybody wants something
What if it's the same thing?

[Verse]
Typical platform, everybody pulls apart
Users want cheap transactions from the start
Developers want adoption for their apps
Miners want income, holders want the price up, facts
More adoption don't make transactions cheap
More demand on the chain and the fees get steep
Cheaper transactions, miners don't earn more
Not aligned, often in conflict, that's the score

[Chorus]
Same side, same side
Higher price and everybody rides
Network more secure, miners get paid
Holders get the return, same side, made

[Verse]
On C K B the users want their assets secure
Developers want more assets preserved, for sure
Miners want income, holders appreciation
Higher token price supports the whole equation
More assets secured, more bytes occupied
Circulating supply goes down, price has support on its side
Miners expand, the network's more secure
Draws higher value usage, more and more
Pro-cyclical loop, that's the growth engine
Adoption and value, each one extending
First class assets, cells at the top
Owned by the user, lock script, full stop
Not held in custody by a contract's hand
So the storage cost's on the users, understand
Four hundred bytes of code for a token's rules
Sixty-four bytes per owner, those are the tools
Ten thousand owners, the developer still
Needs four hundred C K Bytes, that's the bill

[Chorus]
Same side, same side
Higher price and everybody rides
Network more secure, miners get paid
Holders get the return, same side, made

tracks.title: Borrowed Bytes
tracks.source: RFC 15 §7-8 Lending, subscriptions and liquidity income
tracks.lyrics:
[Intro]
Lend it out, lock it in
Bytes come back again

[Verse]
Utility's in holding, not in the send
So here's a thing that you can do, lend
C K Bytes locked for a known time span
Risk-free, no collateral, that's the plan
Entrepreneur borrows for six months, say
Builds a prototype, proves it'll pay
Lower capital cost to start
Long term users lend and earn their part
Rate's set by supply and demand
And how much of the state's in hand

[Chorus]
Borrowed bytes, borrowed bytes
High use, high rate, release the state tonight
Low use, low rate, come build it right
Borrowed bytes, borrowed bytes

[Verse]
High utilisation, fewer bytes to lend
Interest goes up, and that's the trend
Makes it worth it to release your state
Lock in the Dao and collect the rate
Low utilisation, more bytes around
Interest drops, and adoption's found
Subscriptions, that's another block to build
Lock in the Dao and the service gets billed
Provider's the beneficiary of the interest paid
Withdraw from the Dao and the service fades
Store of assets users, same idea
Subscription metered by state size, clear
Miners the beneficiary, security's the service
Layer two operators, here's another purpose
Fixed deposits lent to the market for income
On top of the layer two fees, and then some

[Chorus]
Borrowed bytes, borrowed bytes
High use, high rate, release the state tonight
Low use, low rate, come build it right
Borrowed bytes, borrowed bytes

[Outro]
Base layer, most secure and the highest cost
Built for high value and the long term, boss
